text:
olivia (customer): hey team - starting ~10:12 UTC our hosted inference endpoint kept returning 502/504s for several clients. seen in us-west region mainly. sample request id: rq_0a1b2c3d4e. latency spikes then gateway errors. customer impact: multiple pods in prod failing simple generate calls. can provide logs.

maya (support): sorry to hear that olivia. can you paste a curl that reproduces? and which model/route? any client-side TLS errors?

olivia (customer): curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -d '{"model":"rw-base","prompt":"test"}'

* curl output pasted: *
* About to connect() to api.redwood.ai port 443 (#0)
*   Trying 54.23.11.9... connected.
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (54.23.11.9) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake: stalled, then "SSL connection timeout"
* Related HTTP code: 000
* Closing connection 0

olivia (customer): Also in our server logs we see downstream 502 from gateway with message "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers".

maya (support): thx. tagging sre. @lee can you take a look at edge traces?

lee (sre): on it. pulling proxy logs and TLS logs for us-west. can you confirm whether customers see cert mismatch or handshake timeouts?

olivia (customer): we only see timeouts + 502s. nothing obvious about cert name mismatch on client side.

lee (sre): seeing spikes in handshake timeouts from our edge pool in us-west-2 between 10:10-10:30 UTC. hits seem to correlate with DNS resolution errors from some resolver clusters. examples from edge logs:

```
[2026-03-14T10:15:23Z] proxy[edge-usw2-03]: TLS handshake timeout after 7s for upstream api-host-abc01.redwood.internal
[2026-03-14T10:15:23Z] proxy[edge-usw2-03]: upstream connect error: TLS handshake failed: alert handshake_failure
[2026-03-14T10:15:23Z] dns-resolver[edge-usw2-03]: query api.redwood.ai -> SERVFAIL (server failure)
```

lee (sre): running dig from a repro machine in same AZ gives intermittent SERVFAIL:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.ai @1.1.1.1
# sometimes returns CNAME -> edge-xyz.redwood.net
# sometimes returns ;; -> SERVFAIL
```

aj (eng-runtime): hmm. we rolled cert rotation for a few edge LB pools at 10:05 UTC (canary then wider). deploy-bot shows cert rotation job finished by 10:08. @deploy-bot can you confirm rollout plan?

deploy-bot: cert-rotation-job-2026-03-14 completed: canary -> 3/5 pools -> full-rollout started. rolling certs patch: apply new intermediate chain + OCSP staple refresh. No rollback triggered.

maya (support): could this be OCSP stapling or incomplete chain where some resolvers get a CNAME to old backend that no longer presents full chain?

lee (sre): possible. I’m seeing two behaviors:
- resolver returning old CNAMEs that point at edge instances which no longer have the previous cert chain (handshake failure).
- resolver returning SERVFAIL for some queries, causing proxy to fallback to different pools and then time out.

aj (eng-runtime): running openssl s_client to the failing IP shows missing intermediate on some backends:

```
$ openssl s_client -connect 54.23.11.9:443 -servername api.redwood.ai -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = api.redwood.ai
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.redwood.ai
   i:/CN=Intermediate-Old
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIID...oldintermediate...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----
```

aj (eng-runtime): other IPs show the new intermediate. suggests an inconsistent cert rollout across edge pool or DNS caching returning old targets.

lee (sre): i've also traced that several resolver clusters had their cache TTL much longer than expected for the CNAME records (explicitly 5m but some caches honor older TTL). DNS provider reported they served some stale answers while they were failing over.

maya (support): what's the mitigation scope? customer needs stable API.

aj (eng-runtime): immediate mitigations:
- temporarily route traffic for affected tenants in us-west to our fallback pool (edge-alt) that has validated cert chain. applying rule now for olivia's customer id.
- clear local resolver caches on edge nodes where possible and drop EDNS caching to force fresh lookups.
- contact DNS provider to purge stale cache and confirm NO_SERVFAIL behaviour.

lee (sre): applied route override for olivia's customer at 10:40 UTC -> observed success on their side: no more 502s. olivia can you confirm?

olivia (customer): got green from a few clients. thanks. still seeing a minority of clients hit 504s but much reduced.

maya (support): nice. I'm going to keep the thread open until DNS provider confirms full purge and until rotation verifies. @dns-bot can you run a global probe for api.redwood.ai and post aggregation?

dns-bot: global probe summary (10:05-11:00 UTC):
- 12/20 probes returned correct CNAME -> edge-alt.redwood.net + good chain
- 6/20 probes returned CNAME -> edge-old.redwood.net with old intermediate
- 2/20 probes returned SERVFAIL

aj (eng-runtime): we've asked DNS provider to purge caches and push a forced TTL refresh. they acknowledged and started process at 10:45 UTC. will monitor.

lee (sre): longer term action items:
- tighten cert rotation canary to ensure no mixed-chain state visible to DNS caching.
- add healthcheck that verifies intermediate chain presence post-rotation.
- hunt for any resolvers honoring stale negative caching longer than allowed.

maya (support): logged a ticket with DNS provider (ticket 765432) and cc'd infra. keeping customer in the loop while we monitor. olivia, we'll send a postmortem when stable.

olivia (customer): thanks team. appreciate rapid mitigation and route override. please cc me on the postmortem and any followups.

aj (eng-runtime): note for postmortem: probable root cause = cert rotation + DNS caching leading to mixed chain visibility across resolvers causing TLS handshake failures and intermittent SERVFAILs. mitigation = route override + DNS purge.

lee (sre): closing short-term incident after stability window. will reopen if error rates climb above baseline. metrics show 95% reduction in 502/504s for affected customers after override.

maya (support): assigning followups to eng-runtime and dns infra. leaving thread open for 24h. :thumbsup:

olivia (customer): confirmed - all good for now. thanks again!
